analysis.title: Keysight Technologies Inc. (KEYS): Record orders with strong growth drivers for FY27 and beyond; 4QFY26 wrap
key_insights: KEYS 4QFY26 revenue was $1,994 mn (up 8% qoq, up 41% yoy), versus GS $1,948 mn and Street (FactSet) $1,946 mn, and above the top of the $1,930-1,950 mn guidance range. Core revenue was up 36% yoy.
Non-GAAP EPS ex-SBC was $3.61 versus GS $3.39 and Street $3.37, above the $3.34-3.40 guidance range. Non-GAAP EBIT margin ex-SBC was 35.8% versus Street 34.5% and GS 35.0%.

Orders were a record $2,339 mn (up 12% qoq, up 53% yoy as reported, up 49% yoy organically) with a book-to-bill of 1.17X. The 12% qoq growth is within typical seasonality. GS thinks some investors may have expected more given strong end demand, but the 3Q base was also high.
1QFY27 guidance is revenue of $2,040-2,060 mn and non-GAAP EPS ex-SBC of $3.63-3.69. Midpoints are $2.05 bn and $3.66, versus Street $1.96 bn and $3.21 and GS prior $1.93 bn and $3.08.

Keysight guides FY27 revenue growth of about 20% as a base case, implying ~$8.6 bn versus GS prior ~$8.1 bn and Street ~$8.2 bn. Management expects FY27 incremental margins in the mid-to-high 40% range, above its 40% long-term framework.

Management expects 1QFY27 orders to decline mid-single digits sequentially, consistent with seasonality, and says this does not reflect a demand change. The company enters FY27 with a record backlog and strong pipeline.
AI bookings in FY26 were ~2.5x FY25. GS estimates this implies about $1.4 bn in FY26.
Demand continues to outpace supply. Capacity has increased for the fourth consecutive quarter, but management calls fully easing supply constraints a moving target.

GS sees long-term growth beyond FY27 from 6G R&D (6G slated to come online in 2029 per management), aerospace and defense projects, and optical interconnect programs. Recurring revenue was 25% of total in the quarter.
GS raises FY27/28 EPS (inc. SBC) to $13.95/$15.45 from $12.50/$14.05 and introduces FY29 at $16.45. Ex-SBC EPS is $15.40/$16.95/$18.00 for FY27/28/29.
GS cuts its 12-month price target to $464 from $487, now based on 30X (from 35X, reflecting peer multiples) normalized EPS of $15.45 inc. SBC. Rating stays Buy, with 64.9% upside from $281.42.

market_movers.rationale: Maintains Buy after a 4QFY26 beat, record orders and guidance above the Street. The target falls from $487 because the multiple drops to 30X from 35X, partly offset by higher EPS estimates.

earnings_insights: 4QFY26 (reported 11/19/2026): revenue $1,994 mn actual vs GS $1,948 mn and Street (FactSet) $1,946 mn. Non-GAAP EPS ex-SBC $3.61 actual vs GS $3.39 and Street $3.37. Non-GAAP EPS inc. SBC $3.35 actual vs GS $3.07.
4QFY26 non-GAAP operating income ex-SBC was $714 mn (35.8% margin) vs GS $681.8 mn (35.0%) and Street $672 mn (34.5%). Inc. SBC it was $669 mn (33.6% margin) vs GS 32.2%.

4QFY26 segment orders: Commercial Communications $1,145 mn, Electronic Industrial Solutions $498 mn, Aerospace, Defense & Government $351 mn. GS estimates were $1,061 mn, $521 mn and $366 mn, so Communications beat by 7.9% and the other two missed by 4.4% and 4.1%.
Free cash flow was about $465 mn, ~23% of revenue. Software and services were ~33% of revenue.
1QFY27 guidance (company, issued with 4Q results): revenue midpoint $2,050 mn vs GS prior $1,927 mn and Street $1,963 mn. Non-GAAP EPS ex-SBC midpoint $3.66 vs GS prior $3.08 and Street $3.21.
FY27 guidance (company): ~20% revenue growth, ~$8.6 bn. GS new FY27E revenue is $8,641 mn vs $8,123 mn prior, and FY28E is $9,304 mn vs $8,728 mn prior.
risk_factors: Revenue could be lower than GS estimates in 5G/6G, EVs/AVs and 800Gb/1.6Tb/3.2Tb on weaker end-market trends or share shifts.
Margins could face pricing pressure, tariffs, or the shift to production test, despite the expected software mix benefit.
Keysight's ability to keep innovating and leading through R&D and M&A.
